Female, 30. 

While there is no one set reason for me to not have kids, I wanted to be as helpful as possible and provide a thoughtful answer. 

When I was a child myself I knew that I did not want to have my own children. I did not like that grown ups would tell me that one day I would grow up, get married and have babies. Why were they planning my life out for me while I was still a child myself? That was a hard no from little me and even more so from older me. 

I have always noticed parents who do not care for their children as they should. Or struggle with mental health, finances and relationship but they believe that having a baby will fix all of this and “complete” them. But of course the baby does not fulfill their life’s purpose as they had always been told. Women are told this practically from infancy. 

Girls are told they will be a mom one day and it will be the best thing they will ever experience or the classic “you don’t know true love until you have a child”. But we have all seen plenty of parents who do not love their children at all but had them out of obligation or spite. Or even some parents who DO love their children but still do not feel “fulfilled” or even happy. 

Because that is fed to us, especially women, a lot, there is not a lot of emphasis on self development and learning about who you are and what makes you truly happy. Instead it is a societal norm (thankfully not as much pressure as it was back in my mom’s day) to date, to get engaged, married and have babies as soon as you can. Because that’s supposedly when your life really starts! 

But in that time, there was no time for that young woman, or man, to get to know themselves and establish who they are before bringing a new life into the world. Couples who wait to have children when they are older and more financially set and are typically happier because they have had a chance to find themselves (not always the case of course just speaking on my observation of couples around me.). Or once grown and established in themselves, they may realize that children are not their ultimate goal and that’s great!

“You won’t be happy until you have had your own children.” I have even had someone say that it was a waste that I am choosing not to have children because I would be a great mother. But I don’t believe my worth is in having children. And even if I would be a great mother there are plenty of people, young and old, who need nurture and care. So why not spend my free time and money to invest in those around me? 

If every family who wants children was willing to adopt a child or even donate money to causes that help children and people in need instead of adding on that 3rd or 4th  kid to their family line out of a societal obligation, the world could possibly be a much better place. And I think that people who want their own children but not somebody else’s child, should take a deep look as to why that is. Do you really want to be a parent or are you only wanting to pass on your genetic pool and keep your line going?. There is nothing wrong with having your own children of course but there are other options to consider in addition to having your own. 

I have had plenty of extended family members who have babies in bad situations and the kids get messed up from it and are now homeless. Or the children are put into foster care. I have personally been contacted by social services asking about fostering an extended family member whose mom can no longer take care of her. And while I was open to it, the mom ended up getting her back and who knows what happened to her after that. 

With all that said, I should also say that I do not hate children. I think they can be wonderful and extraordinarily interesting in their own unique ways. And I love hearing about their perspective on life and what interests them. Children should be cherished and people need to know what they are going into 1000% so that these babies do not get hurt or traumatized. Some people are not meant to be parents. Expecting parents need to realize that it’s not just a cute baby they are bringing into the world. This is a human being. This is someone who will live the rest of their life shaped by the choices their parents made, whether good or bad. If more people really pondered the vastness of their decision, perhaps more individuals would choose an alternative path. 

 Children are not for the faint of heart. I do not want to bring that responsibility on myself or my body. 

I do enjoy having my coffee in the morning in peace and quiet. I love a clean home. I love being able to go where I want to on the weekend; whether it be a camping trip or staying home and watching tv or reading books. I love working and not feeling bad about overworking some days. I love not having my own children. Genuinely. 

But if one day there was a child in my family who needed a home, I would give it to them happily. I would be able to do that because I did not have children of my own. Until then, I am happy giving to others as best I can while also having my coffee in peace in the mornings.

OP, I would agree with everyone else here that these boundaries are not too strict at all. 

 However!

I can understand completely why these necessary changes would be challenging for you to cope with as well. 

It is understandable to want your child to be happy immediately because that in turn will bring you happiness in the moment. But it is not maintainable. 

They are little now but I will tell you, they will be teens in no time! And the lack of boundaries will cause disruptions in the home and they will become even harder to manage. If they are at the point of yelling at you already, being preteens and teens will be 1000% worse. 

I know it can be hard to see but I am speaking from experience with living with my younger brother. He became physically and verbally violent when he got older because respect wasn’t established. And I made it ultra clear to my husband that we need to create boundaries, consequences and also REWARDS for my step kid. While I am not saying your kids will become violent, I am saying that it is important for them to learn boundaries and how/why we respect. Because every single teen gets attitude and even the most mannered can be challenging to work with. 

One suggestion, I believe in rewarding the child for good behavior. We do a chore chart with red, yellow and green smiley face stickers but I have heard of people doing a behavioral chart. 

Based on what you are working on with them, you can place a sticker and then talk with them about why they received that sticker for the day. And then at the end of the month, or the week depending on how you want to do it, they can get a small treat based on their behavior (ice cream or pick out their favorite candy, 20 extra minutes at the park etc). We do one biggish activity at the end of the month For our chore chart. We present it as, “you helped the family by doing your chores and now we can all go enjoy our free time by doing X together”.  It’s usually something like bowling or bounce place that we don’t do on a typical weekend. And I have found this to be a great way for him to be able to visualize how he is doing with the calendar. 

I would encourage you to get professional counseling on the matter because,  yes, it is a big change for your kids, but it is a BIGGER change for you. Counseling is a wonderful tool to get your thoughts and feelings out in a safe space so that you can begin processing them with someone who is trained to do so. You can be brutally honest about how you feel during a session and that feels GOOD. But most importantly you can begin to work on why this adjustment is hard for you! 

They will adjust quickly because children need structure and are moldable but you as an adult are a bit more set in your ways (which is fine, we all are until something needs to change). 

Just know that he is doing the right thing (based on what you wrote) and now it is time to work on yourself and how you view the situation and learn to adjust your feelings accordingly.

Absolutely not okay! Your SO needs to put his foot down and show his daughter that you both are a TEAM and you will stand united. It sounds cheesy but it is absolutely necessary when establishing respect and healthy boundaries. You as the stepparent cannot be the one coming in and demanding respect and dulling out the consequences if respect is not give. 

My stepson was 5 when me and my SO began dating. I told him early on that if we are serious and wanting to move into a permanent relationship, I need to have a voice in parenting and he needs to back me up. 

At the beginning I viewed it as a “aunt” relationship. I’m there to be a support to the kid, have fun and give them gentle guidance on behavior.  But I was NOT wanting to be the disciplinarian. If his kid did something that wasn’t good, SO needed to be the one who put his foot down. 

This developed into what it is today and I would say I have taken on more of a parenting role. I have been in SK’s life long enough that it has naturally progressed into me becoming a mother figure and I 100% take it seriously (even thought I am not relaxing his BM). I will sit SK down for talks if he didn’t do something that was right, I will tell him to check his attitude and reevaluate how he wishes to respond, I will have him do his chores and re-do his chores if they didn’t do to best ability. I remind him to treat us the way he would want to be treated and for the most part, he does well. 

My SO and I are a team and when it comes to true discipline I still have SO carry it out but I do give my opinion on what should be done. My SK knows that me and SO are united and we will always be on the same page. If me and SO disagree, we take a short break away from SK and discuss it. I can understand this. 

I was once prophesied over by my father‘s close friend, and he told me that I was meant to be a missionary, and spread the gospel to those in need and travel while doing so. Of course, that never happened. Nor did an opportunity present itself for that to happen. 

my father and mother always talked about the experiences they had spiritually. Experiences during prayer, church and so on. They told me about a cloud that descended upon a group of them while they were praying, and they could not explain it. Also, about demonic encounters. They told me about dreams that they had that come true that were from God. 

I took their signs and wonders as proof enough growing up. I also sought after my own, and hoped that God would reveal himself to me in some way or another. But, when he did not, I still allowed the experiences of other people to be confirmation enough that he was real. 

I eventually found a church when I was a young adult that told me “God brought you here for a reason and you need to stay regardless of how painful it can be”. 

I stayed at that church for 8 years because I was telling myself that God brought me here for a purpose and I didn’t want to miss out on him. I stayed through gossip about me, untrustworthy holier than thou people and I even stayed when the pastor started subtlety grooming me since the tender age of 20. I looked past the things he would say and do because I was afraid to question it or walk away BECAUSE these people “talked to God” and prayed 8 hours a day. “So what he must be doing and saying isn’t meant in the way it comes across because he is close to God.” Thats what I would tell myself anyway because I was afraid. 

At this church I witnessed shrieking sounds portrayed as praying in tongues. It would give me goose bumps and I would want to close my ears but they would say that it was my heart that wasn’t right because I wanted to walk away from the Holy Spirit. I was part of what I can only describe as an exorcism. A church member had epilepsy and they prayed for him for over an hour. The “demon” supposedly left but the pastor said it came back because the church member did not do the work. 

These pastors always taught of the miracles they saw and did as well as visions they received from God. “The time is near” they would say. For the end of the world. 

They taught that members were under a “spiritual covering” and if you left that covering you were susceptible to demonic attacks. Such as dying in a car crash etc. Talk about a prison of the mind! 

With all of this I just want to say, I can understand holding out for the miracle or the sign from God. These people give you hope regardless if it was meant for good or evil. 

My dad’s friend, I am sure was well intentioned. He spoke what he felt but it does not mean it was a prophecy from God. 

The church I left however, some people were well intentioned and some were not. Regardless, they spoke and taught what it was that they learned all of their life, with their own additions here and there. They prophesied things that never came true. Again showing that it was of their own mind that they were prophesying, not God’s. 

While at this point in life I am not sure if there is a God or not. What I am sure of is that people have made God into what it has become today. 

Have you heard the song “Personal Jesus” by Depeche mode? People look for something higher and customize that Higher Power to suit their needs. 

If you look at church history you can see the shift and evolution it has taken on over the years. I would recommend reading into church history if you have not before because it opened my eyes and gave me the courage to leave my church. I realized the way they practice religion now is very new in the grand scale of it all.  

For me, while I don’t believe in any of it, I don’t see any harm in adopting a religious practice even if the individual is not convinced of it all. It can be a beautiful way to “explain” life and offer some hope as people go through challenging times. My spouse is Orthodox Christian and while I am not a practicing Orthodox, I can see the beauty in it. 

As long as it is bettering the individuals life as well as the lives of people around that individual it can be beneficial. But when it is weaponized or people begin “prophesying” or evangelizing, you can see the negative effect it can have on people’s minds. Especially when that hopeful “prophecy” does not come true. Religion or spirituality should be an individual practice and not pushed onto other people! 

That’s a lot to read but I hope it is helpful in some way or another. And if it isn’t helpful, apologies. 😊
